Repair trial-by-trial JATOS result data into a valid JSON

Source: R/rawdata-jatos.R
repair_jatos_json.Rd

CATLAS experiments stream every jsPsych trial to JATOS as it finishes, via jatos.appendResultData(JSON.stringify(data)). JATOS stores the appended strings back to back, so a study result arrives as a sequence of JSON objects, {...}{...}{...}, with neither the enclosing brackets nor the separating commas that would make it one JSON array. repair_jatos_json() supplies both missing components, so the result can be parsed with jsonlite::fromJSON().

Usage

repair_jatos_json(x)

Arguments

x

Character. One element per JATOS study result, typically the data_raw column of jatosR::process_results()$data. A logical vector of NAs is accepted too and will be returned unchanged.

Value

A character vector of the same length as x. Each element is a JSON array of trial records. NA stays NA, an empty string becomes "[]", and an element that already is a JSON array is returned unchanged.

Details

The repair inserts a comma wherever a closing brace is followed, possibly after whitespace, by an opening brace. It does not parse the JSON, so a string value containing }{ would be split as well. jsPsych escapes quotes but not braces, so this can only happen when a participant types }{ into a free-text field. The record would then fail to parse, which shows up as an invalid result.

Examples

raw <- c(
  '{"trial_type":"consent","response":1}{"trial_type":"stimuli-map"}',
  NA,
  ""
)
repair_jatos_json(raw)
#> [1] "[{\"trial_type\":\"consent\",\"response\":1},{\"trial_type\":\"stimuli-map\"}]"
#> [2] NA                                                                              
#> [3] "[]"
